# Full dispatch follow-up with adjacent controls

Predeclared for #3117: A1/A2 main 551d4d0825dca64b7143d6f18fc2b13baaf1fe0a, B e376956c74b544e961d9e508a5d8402e35765c69. The full prior run 34287951725 retained a pending-record maximum loss and control/runtime transitions in other cases. The new instrumented pending-record pilot 34314229701 meets its end-to-end point screens after correcting a signed-timing analysis error, but is partial and still records runtime transitions. Its exact metrics and limitations are published in PR comment 5596399517 before this follow-up.

Use `dispatch-adjacent` on one ubuntu-latest VM with the same full set of six microbenchmarks, four Kafka modes and four loaded dispatcher shutdown cases. Validate all fourteen configurations against both products before timing. For each identical workload, run A1, B, then A2 immediately before advancing to the next workload. Preserve the complete predeclared execution plan and actual UTC capture order. This reduces separation between controls; it does not average or discard any control.

Each Kafka capture gets 361 seconds offered warmup and 180 seconds offered measurement. Require at least 360 seconds of completed workload warmup. This extends the preceding 121/120-second experiment to exercise more recurring maintenance and thread-pool activity before the measured window. Retain all measured samples and maxima, including any remaining JIT/GC or scheduling transitions. Report INCONCLUSIVE if startup still materially affects results. Every Kafka capture starts a fresh broker and topic, with the same coordinator initialization, input reset and CPU affinity. The source fixtures, rates, record sizes, batching, capacities, runtime/JIT/GC, boundaries and sampler stay identical across the controls and candidate. Handler-stage timing is disabled for the full matrix; its prior diagnostic has a separate recorded observation cost.

Microbenchmarks retain their actual 20-second initial workload warmup, 30 BDN warmup and 25 measured iterations, DontRemove, MemoryDiagnoser and exact zero-allocation steady-dispatch checks. Focused shutdown retains 120 seconds continuous warmup and 60 seconds measurement for every case. These settings and the original workload semantics are documented in EXPERIMENT.md.

No acceptance tolerance changes: micro mean-time loss 1%, micro control drift 2%; loaded completed-throughput/CPU loss 3%, actual-message and loaded-shutdown p50/p99/max loss 5%, allocation increase at most 1 B/message against each control, with separate control-drift checks and exact correctness. Report complete-lifetime allocations separately from steady 0 B/message and cold/amortized costs. JIT/time-series uncertainty and applicable missing metrics remain INCONCLUSIVE. Do not infer long-run leak absence beyond the observed window.

The job has a 350-minute ceiling because the full sequential set includes 108 minutes of Kafka warmup/measurement, focused microbenchmarks, 36 minutes of shutdown samples and both-revision smoke/build/reset overhead. The ceiling does not authorize extra repetitions. Both product binaries and fixture sources are built before timing and retained with exact hashes, hardware/SDK/runtime, all raw samples, runtime series and decision rationale. Main movement is recorded separately without changing pinned revisions mid-run.
